1.e4 e5 2.Nf3 Nc6 3.Bb5 Nf6 4.d3 d6 5.Bx.strategy: Trades the bishop for the knight at once. Because the d-pawn has already moved, Black must recapture with the b-pawn, which doubles the c-pawns and opens the b-file but leaves Black the two bishops. White gets a lasting structural target in return for the bishop pair.
1.e4 e5 2.Nf3 Nc6 3.Bb5 Nf6 4.d3 d6 5.Bx.name: Ruy Lopez: Berlin Defence, Anti-Berlin Variation, Anderssen Variation

1.e4 e5 2.Nf3 Nc6 3.Bb5 Nf6 4.d3 d6 5.c4.strategy: Takes space, covers d5 and supports the bishop on b5 with a pawn. The cost is d4: with pawns on c4 and d3, no White pawn can ever guard it, so it becomes a lasting outpost for Black's pieces. An aggressive try, riskier than the quiet set-ups.
1.e4 e5 2.Nf3 Nc6 3.Bb5 Nf6 4.d3 d6 5.c4.name: Ruy Lopez: Berlin Defence, Anti-Berlin Variation, Duras Variation
